cards.prompt: Your shopping account. Sign of a take-over, or normal?

items.label: A laptop you don't own, signed in
A receipt for something you just bought
A code right after you tapped sign in

cards.explanation: Orders and devices that weren't you are signs of a take-over. A receipt or code that matches what you just did is the account doing its job.

cards.prompt: Your music app is playing songs you never picked. You can still sign in.

choices.text: Tell a trusted adult, and make a new, strong password
choices.consequence: Good start: the old password no longer works.

choices.text: Wait a week to see if it keeps happening
choices.consequence: Every day gives whoever is in your account more time.

choices.text: Make a new account and forget the old one
choices.consequence: The attacker keeps the old account, and may try that password elsewhere.

steps.text: In the settings, the recovery email is one you've never seen. What now?

choices.text: Remove it and add your own
choices.consequence: Now nobody else can reset your new password.

choices.text: Leave it: you've already changed the password
choices.consequence: Whoever owns that email could use it to reset your new password.

cards.explanation: Tell a trusted adult and change the password first. Then remove any recovery email that isn't yours, so the attacker can't reset the new password.

cards.prompt: Match each problem to where to go.

pairs.left: Someone used your card details online
A fake parcel text to warn others about
Someone could get hurt right now

cards.explanation: Your bank straight away for card details, Scamwatch for scams, 000 for danger right now, and IDCARE for stolen personal details.

cards.prompt: A new number's voice message sounds like your aunt: "Lost my phone! Buy two gift cards and send me the codes, quick."

choices.text: Call your aunt on the number you already have
choices.consequence: She answers, confused: she never lost her phone. It was a voice clone.

choices.text: Buy the cards: it's definitely her voice
choices.consequence: Voices can be copied with AI. Gift card codes are hard to get back once sent.

choices.text: Reply to the new number to ask if it's really her
choices.consequence: The new number belongs to whoever sent it, so of course they'll say yes.

cards.explanation: A new number, hurry and gift card codes are red flags, and a voice can be faked. Check on the number you already have.
Four **random** words are long and unpredictable. Song lyrics, pet names with birth years, and short words with symbol swaps are all guessed early.

cards.prompt: Your password leaked, but you use two-step sign-in with codes from a phone app. What else would an attacker need?

options.text: The code from the app on your phone
Nothing more: the password gets them in
Just your username, which is easy to find

cards.explanation: With two-step sign-in, a stolen password isn't enough: they'd also need the code from your phone. That's why it's worth turning on.

cards.prompt: Your cousin's account messages: "I entered you in a giveaway! A code will arrive by text. Just send it to me."

steps.text: The code arrives. What do you do?

choices.text: Don't send it, and warn your cousin another way
choices.consequence: Right: that code was for signing in to your account.

choices.text: Send it: it's your cousin's account
choices.consequence: That code opens your account, and your cousin's account may have been taken over.

choices.text: Send it, then change your password straight after
choices.consequence: They could be in your account before you change anything. Never send a sign-in code.

cards.explanation: Never send a sign-in code to anyone, even a friend or family member. Their account may have been taken over.

cards.prompt: Someone in a game keeps sending you nasty messages, and it's upsetting you. What's always a good first step?

options.text: Tell a trusted adult what's been happening
Keep it to yourself so it doesn't get bigger
Send one sharp reply so they know to stop

cards.explanation: Telling a trusted adult is always a good first step. It's never your fault, and you don't have to deal with it alone.
